item.text:
**8B.1 Research Note: Sheikh Hasina in 2024**

Bottom line: **yes, the governing program was explicit**. The clearest public line was `Smart Bangladesh by 2041` plus poverty reduction, digitalization, jobs, and governance reform. The **revealed power strategy** was also explicit in practice: keep the election under her administration, reject a neutral authority, and then use curfew and internet shutdowns when challenged. That makes 8B.1 strongly evidenced on both the program and regime-control sides.

**Positive program articulation**
- **AL unveils Smart Bangladesh manifesto** | **BSS** | **December 27, 2023** | [URL](https://www.bssnews.net/news-flash/165179) | Claim: Hasina promised a “developed, prosperous, Smart Bangladesh” by 2041 and a high-middle-income country by 2031. This is the clearest explicit ideology/program statement for the year. | **8B.1**
- **Full-text of the Awami League manifesto** | **BSS** | **December 27, 2023** | [URL](https://www.bssnews.net/news/165180) | Claim: the manifesto set out specific targets and named four pillars for Smart Bangladesh, while also promising stronger transparency, accountability, democracy, rule of law, human rights, and social equality. This is direct evidence of a concrete governing program that can be evaluated later against action. | **8B.1**
- **Official document: govt to include Smart Bangladesh in mid-term dev plan** | **Dhaka Tribune** | **April 16, 2024** | [URL](https://www.dhakatribune.com/amp/bangladesh/344095/official-document-govt-to-include-smart) | Claim: the planning commission sought to embed Smart Bangladesh into the Ninth Five Year Plan, along with upper-middle-income status by 2031, macro stability, inflation control, employment, poverty alleviation, balanced regional development, and rule of law. This is strong evidence that the slogan was being operationalized as a state strategy. | **8B.1**
- **Govt adopts plan to turn public welfare services into smart services in two years** | **UNB** | **June 4, 2024** | [URL](https://www.unb.com.bd/category/Bangladesh/govt-adopts-plan-to-turn-public-welfare-services-into-smart-services-in-two-years/136812) | Claim: the government moved 52 ministries and divisions into a Smart Bangladesh implementation platform for “smart” public welfare services. This shows the program was not just rhetorical; it had administrative implementation. | **8B.1**

**Revealed power / control goals**
- **Reuters: opposition refusal to accept neutral authority** | **Reuters** | **January 4, 2024** | [URL](https://theprint.in/world/little-election-fizz-in-bangladesh-as-prime-minister-set-for-another-term/1910693/) | Claim: Reuters reported that the opposition boycott followed Hasina’s refusal to resign and let a neutral authority run the election. That reveals a power goal of keeping control over the electoral apparatus rather than making succession genuinely contestable. | **8B.1**
- **Bangladesh turnout low in election set to keep PM Hasina in power** | **Reuters** | **January 7, 2024** | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-turnout-low-in-election-set-to-keep-pm-hasina-in-power-3268699) | Claim: Reuters described the contest as one set to keep Hasina in power, with boycott, low turnout, and allegations of one-party rule. This is direct evidence that the political program included regime preservation, not just policy goals. | **8B.1**
- **Sheikh Hasina wins fifth term amid turnout controversy** | **Al Jazeera** | **January 8, 2024** | [URL](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/1/8/sheikh-hasina-wins-fifth-term-in-bangladesh-amid-turnout-controversy) | Claim: Al Jazeera reported “dummy candidates” and described the vote as a “dummy election” that would return Hasina to power. This is strong evidence of an explicit strategy to preserve parliamentary control while preserving a competitive veneer. | **8B.1**
- **Bangladesh army enforces curfew as student-led protests spiral** | **Reuters** | **July 20, 2024** | [URL](https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-student-led-protests-spiral/2182818/) | Claim: the government responded to protest escalation with curfew, troop deployment, and internet/text shutdowns. That reveals a regime-control reflex under stress, useful for evaluating the gap between the program’s democratic language and later coercive action. | **8B.1**
- **Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain** | **Reuters** | **July 22, 2024** | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153) | Claim: Hasina publicly blamed political opponents and kept the curfew in place. That is direct revealed-goal evidence of blame-shifting and regime defense rather than neutral crisis management. | **8B.1**
- **Exclusive: army refused to suppress protest, sealing Hasina’s fate** | **Reuters** | **August 6, 2024** | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/exclusivebangladesh-army-refused-to-suppress-protest-sealing-hasinas-fate-3558302) | Claim: Reuters reported the army decided not to fire on civilians to enforce the curfew. This implies Hasina’s survival strategy depended on coercion, and the coercive option only failed because the military refused. | **8B.1**

**Search gap**
- I found **clear programmatic language** in the manifesto, planning documents, and “smart services” rollout.
- I did **not** find a separate 2024 doctrinal paper that cleanly states a hidden theory of regime control; that part has to be inferred from election behavior, the neutral-authority refusal, and the July crackdown.
- The best-supported reading is therefore: **explicit development-state ideology on paper, with strong revealed incentives to preserve personalized control in practice**.
